# IdiotProof — User Stories
> ✅ done (shipped & tested) · 🟡 partial · ⬜ planned. Every ✅ cites the test.
> "Done" = proven by a test that runs in `IdiotProof.slnx` (see [BIBLE §6](BIBLE.md#IP-§6)).

## Epic A — Risk Guardian (the final gate)
- **IP-US-A1 ✅** As a trader, I am blocked from placing any trade without a stop loss, so I can
  never enter open-ended risk. *Given a setup with no stop, When validated, Then it is blocked.*
  *(verified by `ValidateTrade_NoStopLoss_IsBlocked`.)*
- **IP-US-A2 ✅** As a trader, a stop on the wrong side of entry is rejected, so a "stop" can't
  amplify my loss. *(verified by `ValidateTrade_LongStopAboveEntry_IsBlocked`,
  `ValidateTrade_ShortStopBelowEntry_IsBlocked`.)*
- **IP-US-A3 ✅** As a trader, a trade whose risk exceeds my per-trade cap is blocked and an
  adjusted quantity is suggested, so I stay within my limit. *(verified by
  `ValidateTrade_RiskExceedsMaxLossPerTrade_IsBlocked_AndSuggestsAdjustedQty`.)*
- **IP-US-A4 ✅** As a trader, micro-stops and absurdly wide stops are both rejected, so noise
  and over-exposure are excluded. *(verified by `ValidateTrade_StopTooTight_IsBlocked`,
  `ValidateTrade_StopTooWide_IsBlocked`.)*
- **IP-US-A5 ✅** As a trader, a trade risking too much of my account is blocked, so a single
  trade can't endanger the account. *(verified by `ValidateTrade_AccountRiskTooHigh_IsBlocked`.)*
- **IP-US-A6 ✅** As a trader, once my daily loss limit is hit, further trades are blocked
  (circuit breaker), so a bad day can't compound — and a completed trade's loss counts toward
  today's total even if it's the Guardian's very first interaction of the day (an exit with no
  prior entry check that day). *(verified by `ValidateTrade_DailyLossAlreadyExceeded_IsBlocked`,
  `RecordTradePnL_AsFirstEverCall_InitializesDailyLossWithoutValidateTrade`,
  `RecordTradePnL_ThenValidateTrade_SameDay_ReflectsAccumulatedLoss`.)*
- **IP-US-A7 ✅** As a trader, a well-formed setup is approved (with a warning on poor R:R), so
  the guardian doesn't block good trades. *(verified by `ValidateTrade_WellFormedSetup_IsApproved`,
  `ValidateTrade_LowRiskRewardRatio_ApprovesWithWarning`.)*
- **IP-US-A8 ✅** As a trader, the guardian sizes the max quantity against my per-trade cap,
  account percent, and remaining daily risk, so position size is always derived from my limits.
  *(verified by `CalculateMaxQuantity_RespectsPerTradeCap`, `_RespectsAccountPercent`,
  `_RespectsRemainingDailyRisk`, `_NoRiskPerShare_ReturnsZero`.)* — implements [IP-LAW-2](BIBLE.md#IP-LAW-2).

## Epic B — Unattended Monitor loop
- **IP-US-B1 ✅** As a trader, the Monitor keeps running after a tick succeeds and after a tick
  throws, so one bad evaluation never kills the 24/7 loop. *(verified by
  `SuccessfulTick_InvokesOnTickSucceeded`, `FailingTick_InvokesOnTickFailedWithCount_AndContinues`,
  `SuccessAfterFailures_ResetsConsecutiveCounter`.)* — implements [IP-LAW-5](BIBLE.md#IP-LAW-5).
- **IP-US-B2 ✅** As an operator, an external watchdog can detect a hung Monitor via a heartbeat
  file written every tick (success or failure). *(verified by `HeartbeatFile_IsWrittenAfterSuccessfulTick`,
  `HeartbeatFile_RecordsFailure`.)*
- **IP-US-B3 ✅** As an operator, the Monitor shuts down cleanly on cancellation rather than
  crashing. *(verified by `Cancellation_ExitsCleanly`,
  `TickThrowingOperationCanceled_DuringCancellation_ExitsCleanly`.)*

## Epic C — IdiotScript DSL & backtesting
- **IP-US-C1 ✅** As a trader, every sample IdiotScript builds with a long direction, stop, and
  targets, so the DSL surface is internally consistent. *(verified by
  `AllSamples_Build_WithLongDirection_StopAndTargets`.)*
- **IP-US-C2 ✅** As a trader, a script round-trips (parse → serialize → re-parse) preserving
  VWAP/EMA-stack conditions, notional sizing, and multi-target take-profit + stop, so editing
  never silently drops my intent. *(verified by `RoundTrip_PreservesVwapAndEmaStackConditions`,
  `RoundTrip_PreservesNotionalSizing`, `RoundTrip_PreservesMultiTargetTakeProfitAndStop`,
  `NciScript_ParsesBack_WithBreakoutPullbackTargetsAndStop`.)*
- **IP-US-C3 ✅** As a trader, the backtester runs over every sample without error and produces
  trades only when triggers actually fire. *(verified by `Backtest_RunsOnEverySample_WithoutError`,
  `Backtest_NciBreakoutTrigger_FiresWhenPriceCrossesLevel`, `NoBreakout_FiresNoTriggers_AndTradesNothing`.)*
- **IP-US-C4 ✅** As a trader, breakout-then-pullback fires both triggers and hits its target;
  a hit stop produces a losing trade; multi-target scales out across fills; a cycle can repeat;
  an open position closes at end of session. *(verified by
  `Breakout_Then_Pullback_FiresBothTriggers_AndHitsTarget`, `StopLoss_ProducesLosingTrade`,
  `MultiTarget_ScalesOut_AcrossTwoFills`, `Repeat_AllowsASecondCycle`,
  `OpenPosition_ClosesAtEndOfSession_WhenNeitherStopNorTargetHit`.)*
- **IP-US-C5 ✅** As a developer, a backtest over no candles returns an empty report without
  throwing. *(verified by `Run_OnEmptyCandles_ReturnsEmptyReport_NoThrow`.)*

## Epic D — Indicator math
- **IP-US-D1 ✅** As a strategy author, RSI is bounded 0–100 (100 on all gains, 0 on all losses),
  same-length as input, and empty-safe. *(verified by `RSI_AllGains_Returns100`, `RSI_AllLosses_Returns0`,
  `RSI_MixedData_InRange`, `RSI_ReturnsSameLengthAsInput`, `RSI_EmptyInput_ReturnsEmpty`.)*
- **IP-US-D2 ✅** As a strategy author, EMA/ATR/MACD/VWAP compute correctly (EMA period-1 equals
  close and smooths price; ATR scales with volatility; MACD histogram = MACD − signal; VWAP equals
  the volume-weighted typical price and resets at the day boundary). *(verified by `EMA_Period1_EqualsClose`,
  `EMA_IsSmoothedVsRawPrice`, `ATR_FlatMarket_IsSmall`, `ATR_HighVolatility_IsLarger`,
  `MACD_Histogram_IsMacdMinusSignal`, `VWAP_EqualVolume_IsAverageTypicalPrice`,
  `VWAP_ResetsAtDayBoundary`, and the `*_ReturnsSameLengthAsInput` family.)*

## Epic K — Gapper: buy the gap at 4AM, sell before the bell {#Epic-K}
> The flagship flow ([BIBLE §4.4](BIBLE.md#IP-§4)).
> Pick up to 3 tickers on the `/gapper` tab, dial in a profile per ticker, queue; the console
> Monitor buys the gap through the three gates in the premarket window and sells it off before
> the 9:30 bell once momentum rolls over.

- **IP-US-K1 ✅** As a trader, I select a gapper profile, dial it in, and the generated
  IdiotScript survives a full parser round trip — every dialed value (session, entry window,
  gap band, volume, price band, notional, stop %, trailing %, giveback + arm time, sell-by)
  reaches the Monitor exactly as I set it. *(verified by
  `GapperScriptFactory_Script_SurvivesParserRoundTrip`, `GapperScriptFactory_OpenEndedGap_EmitsIsGapUp`,
  `GapperProfile_Validate_CatchesBadDialIns` in `IdiotProof.Strategies.Tests/GapperTests.cs`.)*
- **IP-US-K2 ✅** As a trader, gap conditions evaluate against the real previous close and fail
  closed when it is unknown, so an uncomputable gap can never wave a trade through — and the
  previous-close lookup itself picks the right calendar day regardless of what instant a
  daily bar is timestamped at. *(verified by `IsGapUp_FailsClosed_WithoutPreviousClose`,
  `IsGapUp_Passes_WhenGapMeetsThreshold`, `IsGapBetween_EnforcesBandAndFailsClosed`,
  `GetPreviousCloseAsync_UtcMidnightStampedDailyBars_PicksYesterdayNotToday`.)*
- **IP-US-K3 ✅** As a trader, my gapper only hunts entries inside its ET entry window
  (default 04:00–09:00), on the US-market clock regardless of host timezone. *(verified by
  `TimeWindowCondition_GatesOnEasternClock`, `TimeWindowCondition_WrapsOvernightWindows`.)*
- **IP-US-K4 ✅** As a trader, my held gapper is sold off before the bell: hard sell-by time
  always flattens; the momentum-rollover exit (giving back N% of the entry→peak run) arms in
  the final premarket minutes; hard/trailing stops protect the whole hold. *(verified by
  `Exit_PeakGiveback_SellsAfterMomentumRollsOver`, `Exit_PeakGiveback_NotArmedBeforeArmTime`,
  `Exit_SellBy_AlwaysFlatBeforeTheBell`, `Exit_HardStop_TripsOnEntryDrawdown`,
  `Exit_TrailingStop_TripsOffPeakBeforeArmTime`, `Exit_HoldsWhileMomentumIntact`.)*
- **IP-US-K5 ✅** As a trader, premarket orders are limit + DAY + `extended_hours` (Alpaca's
  hard requirement) — anything else is rejected locally instead of silently queueing to 9:30 —
  and the sandbox broker simulates fills into a real position book so the whole loop runs
  keyless. *(verified by `ExtendedHours_MarketOrder_IsRejectedLocally`,
  `ExtendedHours_LimitGtc_IsRejectedLocally`, `Buy_ThenGetPositions_ShowsTheFill`,

- **IP-US-K6 ✅** As a trader, the console Monitor is the one pipeline: it re-reads my queued gappers from SQL every tick (UI edits apply live), streams Alpaca data (websocket bars + last trades, REST backfill, Mock fallback with gap simulation), fires through the three gates, places the entry through `BrokerRouter`, tracks the position on the Strategy row, and exits it via the rollover brain — feeding realized P&L into the RiskGuardian daily circuit breaker. *(verified by `MockGapDay_EntryFires_InPremarket_ThenGivebackExit_BeforeTheBell`, `MockGapDay_HardSellBy_FlattensEvenIfMomentumNeverRollsOver` in `IdiotProof.Strategies.Tests/GapperLifecycleTests.cs`, and the host-level harness `InSession_TheWorkerFires_ThroughTheGateway_AndRecordsTheSandboxFill`, `OutsideTheStrategysSession_TheWorkerEvaluatesNothing_AndPlacesNoOrder`, `OnAWeekend_TheScheduleHibernates_AndNoStrategyIsTouched` in `IdiotProof.Core.Tests/MonitorWorkerHarnessTests.cs`: the hosted MonitorWorker from the Hub DI graph, LocalDB, pinned clock, Sandbox broker.)*

## Epic R — Strategy replay, scanner & ML dataset {#Epic-R}
- **IP-US-R1 ✅** As a trader, I can replay any strategy against a past ET session and see the exact entry→exit round-trips (price, time, P&L, exit reason), evaluated by the same code the live Monitor runs, so a chart hunch is checked against what the rules actually do. *(verified by `ReplaysTheSavedGapper_PersistsTheRun_AndRendersItsPage`, `RthDrive_FiresOnTheFirstBarOfTheRamp_AndTrailsOutWhenItRollsOver`, `EveryRoundTrip_IsPersisted_WithItsFeatureRows` in `IdiotProof.Operations.Tests/Replay`.)*
- **IP-US-R2 ✅** As a trader, I can replay a ticker with no saved strategy by applying a gapper profile — or a built-in repeating momentum strategy — on the fly, so any scanner name is analysable immediately. *(verified by `AFamilyReplay_NeedsNoSavedStrategy_AndNoPagesWritesNoFiles`, `Replay_ReplaysEachSurvivor_AndSavesTheRuns` (classic-gapper profile, no saved strategy), `EveryListedFamily_ResolvesToADefinition`.)*
- **IP-US-R3 ✅** As the platform, every replay is persisted as a ReplayRun row and the whole published archive regenerates from SQL alone (replay-regen), so the database — not the file tree — is authoritative [IP-LAW-7]. *(verified by `RewritesEveryRunPageAndIndex_FromSql`, `ReplaysTheSavedGapper_PersistsTheRun_AndRendersItsPage`.)*
- **IP-US-R4 ✅** As a trader, one scan pulls the morning movers from Alpaca and auto-replays each gapper into the archive, so the board populates itself. *(verified by `ScreensToTheBand_BiggestFirst_WithoutReplaying`, `Replay_ReplaysEachSurvivor_AndSavesTheRuns`.)*
- **IP-US-R5 ✅** As an analyst, I can export the archive to ML-ready CSVs (per-trade features → P&L label, per-bar time series) so the accumulating replays can train models. *(verified by `WritesTheCsvsAndManifest_FromTheFeatureStore`.)*
- **IP-US-R6 ✅** As a trader, beyond gappers I can replay/scan non-gapper families — a reversal dip-buy (EMA9 reclaim off lows) and an EMA200 trend-break — so range/reversal setups (BE, SPCX, AMD) are analysable too. *(verified by `Reversal_BuysTheEma9ReclaimOffTheLow_NotTheFall`, `EmaBreak_BuysTheEma200Reclaim_AboveVwap` in `ReplayFamilyBehaviorTests`.)*
- **IP-US-R7 ✅** As an analyst, replays land in a normalized SQL feature store (ReplayTrade / ReplayBar) I can query directly (features → win/P&L), not just in CSV blobs, so the dataset is a first-class store. *(verified by `EveryRoundTrip_IsPersisted_WithItsFeatureRows`, `Bars_CarryOhlcvIndicatorsFlagsAndConditionCounts`, `Trades_JoinTheEntryBar_AndComputeDistances` in `ReplayFeaturesTests`.)*
- **IP-US-R8 🟡** As a user, I could link my Alpaca account by OAuth (authorize on Alpaca, store a
  scoped revocable token) instead of pasting a raw key/secret. Foundation shipped
  (AlpacaOAuthClient); endpoints + Bearer broker wiring gated on app registration + paper testing.
 
- **IP-US-R9 ✅** As a trader, I can replay/scan SHORT setups (short a failed high below VWAP), with exit logic mirrored for shorts (stops above entry, cover on a bounce) and P&L inverted, so fade days (NVDA/PANW/BX) are analysable. *(verified by `ShortFade_SellsTheBreakdown_CoversOnTheBounce_AndInvertsPnl`, `ShortFade_StopsOutAboveEntry_AsALoss`.)*
- **IP-US-R10 ✅** As a trader, an RTH open-drive family catches the 9:30 rocket (trend-holding entry: above VWAP + above EMA9 + EMA-stacked), which a crossing trigger misses. *(verified by `RthDrive_FiresOnTheFirstBarOfTheRamp_AndTrailsOutWhenItRollsOver`, `RthDrive_NeverFiresInThePremarket`.)*
- **IP-US-R11 ✅** As a trader, an RSI-oversold-at-support dip-buy family exists (rsireversal) that buys capitulation, not a falling knife: it also requires a confirmed bullish RSI divergence (lower price pivot low, higher RSI pivot low, pivot confirmed 3 bars later). *(verified by `RsiReversalFamily_RequiresConfirmedBullishDivergence_AlongsideOversoldAtSupport`, `RsiReversalFamily_Capitulation_PassesTheDivergenceGate`, `RsiReversalFamily_FallingKnife_FailsTheDivergenceGate`, `Divergence_IsNotSeen_UntilTheSecondPivotIsConfirmed_NoLookahead` in `IdiotProof.Core.Tests/RsiReversalFamilyTests.cs`.)*
- **IP-US-R12 ✅** As a trader, a swing-structure primitive (pivot-based higher-low/lower-high) powers a double-bottom family that buys a confirmed higher low and targets the prior high-of-day (swingreversal + IsHigherLow/IsLowerHigh + ExitAtPriorHigh). *(verified by `SwingReversal_BuysTheConfirmedHigherLow_AndTakesProfitIntoThePriorHigh`.)*

## Epic S — Adaptive auto-strategy generation from observed behavior (planned) {#Epic-S}
> The system watches live price action and AUTO-GENERATES + arms strategies fitted to each
> ticker's own behavior, instead of a human authoring each one. The on-demand gapper generator
> (`auto-gapper` CLI + `AutoGapperScanner` adaptive synthesizer + `AutoGapperScan`/`AutoGapperCandidate`
> feature store) is the working seed. **Design principle: wait for enough information before
> generating** — a trigger in the first thin premarket minutes acts on data that has not locked
> in yet. Nothing here is built beyond the seed.
- **IP-US-S1 🟡** As a trader, "start-of-period quick strategy generation" is a standardized flow:
  at the open of a period the system observes each candidate (volume, range, trend, gap) and
  generates a strategy only once it has *enough* information — never on the first thin minute.
- **IP-US-S2 🟡** As a trader, the biggest payoff is intraday (RTH): the system watches a stock
  plummet and arms a mean-reversion LONG at the low-of-day, and watches a stock soar and arms a
  fade SHORT at the high-of-day — reversion/exhaustion setups the adaptive engine can template.
- **IP-US-S3 🟡** As a trader, each generated strategy's stop/trailing/giveback/size is DETERMINED
  PER TICKER from its observed behavior (price tier, gap size, premarket/RTH volume, ATR), reusing
  the adaptive synthesizer prototyped by the on-demand gapper generator.
- **IP-US-S4 ✅** As the platform, every observation and generation decision (the full feature vector + chosen parameters + arm/skip outcome) is captured to a decision feature store (AutoGapperScan/Candidate, AdaptationDecisions, ExhaustionDecisions), so a model can learn which auto-strategies pay off — joined to the TradeDiary for the realized-P&L label, and checked by `evidence calibration` (predicted probability vs realized win rate, Brier vs base rate). *(verified by `ArmedDecision_GetsRealizedPnL_OnceItsTradeCloses`, `OpenTrade_WaitsForTheExit_BeforeLabeling`, `SkippedDecisions_AndTradesBeforeTheDecision_AreIgnored` in `IdiotProof.Monitor.Tests/ExhaustionOutcomeTests.cs`, the AdaptationDecision outcome join in `AdaptationServiceTests`, `CalibrationTests` and `EvidenceCalibrationOperationTests`.)*

## Epic T — Autonomous market-event research scanner {#Epic-T}
> The `/research` tab is a results review, not a search box: `IdiotProof.ResearchScanner`
> ([BIBLE §4.4](BIBLE.md#IP-§4)), a scheduled, silent console app, sweeps EDGAR/Alpaca/Federal
> Register on its own and ranks what it finds.
- **IP-US-T1 ✅** As a trader, I don't have to type a ticker for the system to find market-moving
  events — a scheduled scan sweeps my watchlist plus a rotating batch of the tracked universe on
  its own. See `TickerUniverseServiceTests`.
- **IP-US-T2 ✅** As a trader, an insider transaction claim reports the actual share count,
  price, and % of holdings changed — not "ownership changed." See `Form4ParserTests`.
- **IP-US-T3 ✅** As a trader, high-value 8-K filings (splits, M&A, material agreements) get their
  real document text fetched automatically instead of generic filing boilerplate, while routine
  8-Ks (director departures, exhibit-only filings) don't cost an extra fetch. See
  `CorporateActionDetectorTests`.
- **IP-US-T4 ✅** As a trader, an exchange rule change that affects many companies (not one
  ticker) shows up as its own macro event, with routine SRO fee-schedule paperwork filtered out
  by an LLM substantiveness check. Proven against the real Nasdaq $5M MVLS continued-listing rule
  in `RegulatoryScannerTests`.
- **IP-US-T5 ✅** As a trader, every claim gets a computed 0-100 significance score (magnitude,
  historical correlation, source trust, recency, watchlist membership) so the feed can rank
  itself instead of me filtering. See `SignificanceScorerTests`.
- **IP-US-T6 ✅** As a trader, claim summaries read like sober equity research — what happened,
  which tickers it affects and why, and when — never clickbait, because the display sentence is
  composed from structured fields rather than trusted as free LLM prose. See the composed-sentence
  assertions in `RegulatoryScannerTests`.
- **IP-US-T7 ⬜** [Retired with the web UI, IP-T504] As a trader, the Research tab's primary view is a significance-ranked feed with a last-scan banner and a 'my watchlist only' toggle, not a search box — built in `Research.razor`; verified by `tests/IdiotProof.Cypress/cypress/e2e/12_research.cy.ts` (banner, watchlist toggle, ranked feed, advanced lookup secondary), green 2026-11-03 against a throwaway LocalDB with `IDIOTPROOF_FAKE_LLM=1` (IP-T382).
- **IP-US-T8 ✅** As a trader, I can trust the significance score means something — the system
  actually checks whether past news correlated with what the stock did next, not just assumes
  it. `OutcomeBackfillService` fetches real price history and marks each old-enough claim
  Realized/Disproven against its Bullish/Bearish call. Proven by `OutcomeBackfillServiceTests`.

## Epic U — Options: buy the idea, sell the hype {#Epic-U}
> Manual single-leg calls and puts on the user's Alpaca account, presented so the premium cost,
> breakeven, and the intrinsic ("real") vs extrinsic ("hype") split are never mental math.
> Separate `/options` section, not the Stock Strategy pipeline ([BIBLE §4.4](BIBLE.md#IP-§4)).
> Manual only: no DSL, Monitor, or RiskGuardian involvement.
- **IP-US-U1 ✅** As a trader, any OCC option symbol (`BE251219C00038000`) is decoded into
  underlying / expiration / right / strike for me — and built back — so I never read one by hand.
  See `OptionContractOccTests`.
- **IP-US-U2 ✅** As a trader, every contract shows its real (intrinsic) value, its hype (extrinsic)
  value in $ and % of premium, its breakeven if held to expiration, days to expiration, and
  moneyness, computed from the live premium. See `IntrinsicValueCalculatorTests`.
- **IP-US-U3 ✅** As a trader, I get a Black-Scholes fair value and an implied volatility even when
  the broker doesn't supply Greeks — solved locally, badged `Model`, textbook-verified, with the
  European-exercise/no-dividend simplifications documented. See `BlackScholesCalculatorTests`.
- **IP-US-U4 ✅** As a trader, the Alpaca options wire format is right before it's ever sent:
  OCC symbol, whole contracts (notional rejected), DAY, no extended hours, Market/Limit only;
  chains page through `next_page_token`; snapshots come from the data host with Greeks/IV left
  null when Alpaca omits them; `us_option` positions decode into contracts. See `AlpacaOptionsWireTests`.
- **IP-US-U5 ✅** As a trader without options approval yet, the Sandbox account serves a realistic
  synthetic chain and fills contracts (× 100) into the position book so I can practise the whole
  flow today. See `SandboxOptionsTests`.
- **IP-US-U6 ✅** As a trader, the `/options` page shows CALLS | strike | PUTS with a colour-ramped
  hype meter per cell, a ticket that spells out "you're buying 2 BE $38 calls for about $1,900; $500
  of that is hype; breakeven $47.50 — you don't have to get there", and my open option positions
  with a real/hype split bar. E2E: `tests/IdiotProof.Cypress/cypress/e2e/08_options.cy.ts`
  (Sandbox: empty state → chain → ticket → confirm → position → close). Presenter math:
  `OptionsPresenterTests`, `OptionPositionViewTests` in `IdiotProof.UI.Tests`.
- **IP-US-U7 ✅** As a trader holding a long option, I'm told when extrinsic value is near its
  recent high AND the research tape is bullish on the underlying — "consider taking profit" —
  informationally, never as an auto-sell. See `SellSignalEvaluatorTests`.
- **IP-US-U8 🟡** As a trader, a Live options order requires the same 5-minute password elevation
  as promoting a strategy to Live, and the ticket locks itself with an explanation while Alpaca
  reports `options_trading_level = 0`. Lock rule proven by `OptionsTradingLevelTests`; field parsing
  by `TradingLevel_ReadsAlpacasPluralFieldNames`. The Live elevation path itself
  (`OptionsLiveElevationModal`) needs a live Alpaca account and is not Cypress-provable — 🟡.
- **IP-US-U9 ✅** As a trader, an announced S&P 500/100 addition or deletion I log in
  `sp-index-events.json` shows up in the Research feed as an `IndexEvent` claim (Bullish for a
  joiner, Bearish for a leaver), Pending until the effective date and then Realized, without
  duplicates on later passes. See `IndexEventScannerTests`.
- **IP-US-U10 🟡** As a trader, a small paper options order round-trips against my real Alpaca
  paper account. Place + cancel proven 2026-09-05 by the opt-in `AlpacaPaperOptionsIntegrationTests`
  (`[Explicit]`, `IdiotProof.Brokers.Tests`): level 3 read, full BE chain + snapshots, one
  buy-to-open limit at $0.01 accepted then cancelled, account flat.
  The fill-and-close half needs market hours and a deliberate user-initiated order — 🟡.
- **IP-US-U11 ✅** As a trader who doesn't speak options, every piece of jargon on the page (call,
  put, strike, hype, breakeven, IV, bid/ask, buy-to-open…) is a dotted word I can hover for a
  one-line hint or click for a plain-English card, and no Alpaca code (`buy_to_open`) ever reaches
  the screen. One source of truth: `OptionsGlossary` (`OptionsGlossaryTests`); rendering:
  `08_options.cy.ts` "explains its jargon".
- **IP-US-U12 ✅** As a trader on a level-1 Alpaca account, the ticket tells me I can't buy a call
  or put outright (covered-only) instead of letting Alpaca reject the order, and the level banner
  shows what each level allows. `OptionsTradingLevelTests`; Sandbox (level 3) path in `08_options.cy.ts`.

## Epic H — Tooling hardening (planned)
- **IP-US-H1 ✅** As a strategy author, IdiotScript parse errors give exact line/column diagnostics with a caret excerpt (unknown verbs with a did-you-mean, unbalanced parens, unterminated strings, a missing Ticker, wrong-type/missing/extra arguments) instead of the tolerant parser silently skipping them, so I can fix a broken script without guessing; dsl validate fails closed on them, and dsl parse, import and the builder show them. ## Epic I — Learning Center {#Epic-I}

> so the docs can never drift from the DSL ([IP-LAW-4](BIBLE.md#IP-LAW-4)). Covers the full
> workflow: Strategy Builder → Monitor → ConditionProgress → three gates → fire. Every section
> below is built in `Learn.razor`; 🟡 until a Cypress spec proves the page.

- **IP-US-I1 ⬜** [Retired with the web UI, IP-T504] As a new trader, I visit `/learn` and see a visual overview diagram of the full IdiotProof workflow (Builder → Monitor → ConditionProgress → three gates → fire), so I understand the system end-to-end before writing my first strategy.
- **IP-US-I2 ⬜** [Retired with the web UI, IP-T504] As a trader, the Learning Center shows the six IdiotScript phases (Setup, Filters, Entry, Order, Risk, Exit) with their reflected verb catalog, so the documentation always matches what the DSL parser actually accepts — implements [IP-LAW-4](BIBLE.md#IP-LAW-4).
- **IP-US-I3 ⬜** [Retired with the web UI, IP-T504] As a trader, I see the three gates (Condition Match → LLM Voter Quorum → Risk Guardian) explained with a visual diagram and plain-English description of what each gate checks and why it can block a fire — implements [IP-LAW-1](BIBLE.md#IP-LAW-1).
- **IP-US-I4 ⬜** [Retired with the web UI, IP-T504] As a trader, the Learning Center shows at least three annotated example strategies (NCI Breakout-Pullback, ERNA AH Momentum, SUNE Wedge Breakout) with each phase highlighted and an 'Open in Builder' link that seeds the describe pane, so I can study and remix a known-good script.
- **IP-US-I5 ⬜** [Retired with the web UI, IP-T504] As a trader, every Learning Center section has a contextual 'try it' link (e.g. 'Try the Builder', 'View Strategies', 'Run a Backtest') so I can move directly from reading to doing without navigating manually.

## Epic J — Backtest UI {#Epic-J}
> Enhances the existing `/backtest` page and `StrategyBacktester.Run()` /
> `BacktestReport` pipeline in `IdiotProof.Strategies`. Adds historical candle fetch,
> per-candle condition pass/fail table, and hypothetical P&L summary. Built in `Backtest.razor`
> + `BacktestReport.ConditionTable`; 🟡 until the Cypress run proves it end to end.

- **IP-US-J1 ✅** As a trader, when I run a backtest for a chosen date, the engine fetches that day's minute-resolution historical candles from Alpaca (Mock when unkeyed) for the strategy's session on the Eastern clock and evaluates the strategy tick-by-tick via `StrategyBacktester.Run()`, so the result reflects real market data and not synthetic candles. *(verified by `SessionWindow_FollowsTheStrategySession_OnTheEasternClock_AcrossDst`, `RunAsync_FetchesTheChosenDaysMinuteCandles_ForTheSession_AndReplaysThem`, `RunAsync_PassesThePreviousClose_SoAGapStrategyCanFire` in `IdiotProof.Core.Tests/BacktestDayRunnerTests.cs`; the /backtest page runs through `BacktestDayRunner`.)*
- **IP-US-J2 ✅** As a trader, the backtest results show a per-candle condition table (timestamp, price, each condition pass/fail column, and whether the signal fired at that candle), so I can see exactly where in the day the strategy triggered or stalled. *(verified by `RunAsync_ReportsAPerCandleConditionTable` in `IdiotProof.Core.Tests/BacktestDayRunnerTests.cs`.)*
- **IP-US-J3 ✅** As a trader, the backtest summary shows total signal count, hypothetical entry/exit prices for each fired trade, and cumulative P&L for the day, so I can judge whether the strategy behaves as expected before enabling it on the live Monitor. *(verified by `RunAsync_SummarizesSignals_EntriesExits_AndPnl` in `IdiotProof.Core.Tests/BacktestDayRunnerTests.cs`.)*

## Epic W — Command line & Hub — drive every IdiotProof service from the CLI and MCP through one Hub
- **IP-US-W1 ✅** As an operator, every IdiotProof capability is one `idiotproof <noun> <verb>` command that is also an MCP tool, generated from one `[Operation]` definition, so the CLI, MCP and docs can never disagree. *(verified by `FromCatalog_EveryOperationBecomesOneUniquelyNamedTool`, `HelpFromJson_IsIdenticalToDescriptorHelp`.)*
- **IP-US-W2 ✅** As an operator, the CLI exits 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 usage, 3 blocked by a gate and 4 confirmation required, so a script or an agent knows exactly what happened. *(verified by `Codes_AreTheContractNumbers`, `Codes_MatchOperationStatus`, `HubDown_IsFailed`.)*
- **IP-US-W3 ✅** As a trader, every order (Monitor entries and exits, CLI and MCP orders, replaces, cancels, closes) goes through one TransactionGateway, so no path can skip the Risk Guardian or the routing rules. *(verified by `Law12_NoProductionCode_CallsABrokerMutator_ButTheGateway`, `Entry_WithoutAStop_IsVetoed`, `Live_ThatResolvesToPaperOrSandbox_IsRefused_NeverDowngraded`.)* — implements [IP-LAW-12](BIBLE.md#IP-LAW-12).
- **IP-US-W4 ✅** As a trader, a Live action from the CLI or MCP only previews and hands back a single-use code bound to that exact order, so an assistant can never move real money without my yes. *(verified by `ManualLive_IssuesACode_ThenConfirmPlacesExactlyThatOrderOnce`, `Confirm_WithADifferentOrderThanPreviewed_IsTampered_AndKeepsTheCode`, `Redeem_ByAnotherUser_IsRefused`, `Redeem_AfterTheLifetime_IsExpired`.)* — implements [IP-LAW-13](BIBLE.md#IP-LAW-13).
- **IP-US-W5 ✅** As an operator, the Hub hosts the Monitor with its leader lease and scanners, so one process runs the trading loop and serves every front door. *(verified by `AddIdiotProofMonitor_HostsTheMonitorWorker_AndTheGraphValidates`.)*
- **IP-US-W6 ✅** As an operator, every CLI and MCP call is written to a command ledger with secrets and account numbers redacted, so I can audit what an assistant did. *(verified by `CommandLedgerRepository_RedactsOnTheWayIn_AndListsNewestFirst`, `RedactArgv_MasksFlagValues_BothForms`.)*
- **IP-US-W7 ✅** As a trader, a strategy prints as a deterministic ASCII stamp I can paste back to recreate it exactly, so I can share or archive a strategy as text. *(verified by `Stamp_IsDeterministic_ForTheSameCanon`, `DifferentStrategies_GetDifferentIdsAndFingerprints`.)*
- **IP-US-W8 ✅** As an assistant, `idiotproof agent bootstrap` tells me the Hub state, owner, catalog and etiquette even when the Hub is down, so every session starts the same way. *(verified by `Bootstrap_WorksOffline`, `Bootstrap_Json`.)*
- **IP-US-W9 ✅** As an assistant, I can search and read the BIBLE, laws, stories, tickets and code docs through `docs search|law|section|story|explain|ticket|dsl`, so I answer from the project instead of guessing. *(verified by `Search_RanksTheLawAboveTheBody_AndRendersATable`, `Type_ShowsDocsLocationMembersAndCallers`, `ShowsDetailCommitsAndHistoryInEt`.)*
- **IP-US-W10 ✅** As an operator, every Alpaca Trading and Market Data endpoint maps to an operation, so the whole Alpaca account is reachable through the Hub. *(verified by `EveryInventoriedEndpoint_HasAnOperationThatExists`, `EveryAlpacaPathTheOperationsCall_IsInventoried`.)*
- **IP-US-W11 ✅** As an operator, the public README and docs never carry a key-shaped string or an account id. *(verified by `ReadmeAndDocsCarryNoKeysOrAccountIdentifiers`.)*
- **IP-US-W12 ⬜** As a trader, the web app runs on the same Hub identity adapters and shows the command ledger and strategy stamps, so the browser and the CLI see the same state.
- **IP-US-W13 ✅** As a trader, fills, cancels and live quotes stream through the Hub (`orders stream`, `market watch`), so an assistant can follow an order without polling. *(verified by `Stream_AuthenticatesListens_ShowsEvents_AndRecordsTheFill`, `Live_PushesEachEventAsItArrives` in `IdiotProof.Operations.Tests/Streaming/OrdersStreamOperationTests.cs`, `Stocks_SubscribeTheChannels_AndRenderTradesQuotesStatusesAndLuld` in `MarketWatchOperationTests.cs`, and `Sse_WritesNamedEvents_OneJsonLineEach` in `OperationStreamTests.cs`.)*

Verified by building IdiotProof.Operations from the worktree's layout with the three files copied in (0 errors), and the full solution in the checkout (IP-T521); 8057c939 Formation alert from the gapper study's validated detector, watch-only (IP-T447, re-scoped by the user): no formation trading rule survived validation (H12 -3.45%/trade, H12p -3.93%, H18 -2.36%), so formation-trigger.json stays all-null and nothing arms. The detector that survived (H11p) is frozen by the new `research gappers detector-export` into Catalogs/formation-detector.json, refit exactly as its validation run (weighted, train only, holdout never read); on export it reproduced the reported weighted AUC 0.912 vs benchmark 0.558 on the same 107,669 validation rows (253,115 train rows) and records each input's train missing share. FormationDetector (Evidence) holds the feature list and row transform now shared by the study's H11/H11p code and the live scorer. At 08:00 ET the recorder scores its universe (FormationDetectorScorer), stores detectorScore on each row and writes one formation-alert audit row with the top 10; its snapshots now also get the reverse-split and 424B/S-1 inputs the study's carried, from the permanent history (FormationReferenceSource, the snapshot stage's rules, cached 10 min). `gapper formation shadow` is the pre-registered 20-session paper shadow (gapper study amendment 06): live rows labeled with the study's own reach label (GapperStudyLabeler.Reach, now shared), detector vs catalyst-latency benchmark AUC with a day-clustered 95% lower bound > 0, and no input missing live 20 points more often than in training. `gapper formation status` shows the detector. Verified in a dev Hub (Monitor off): export, status line and an empty shadow; the live 08:00 path runs only once the recorder is enabled (IP-T447); 22d08560 News and SEC filings read through the permanent history like bars do: HistoryReadThrough serves what IdiotProof_History covers, fetches only uncovered finished ET days (stored and marked covered) and always fetches the current day live (stored, never marked); a stopped history server falls back to the live calls unstored. The gapper radar's catalyst news, ResearchService (8-K, Form 4, news) and the research scan pass use it. Filings come from the issuer's SEC submissions history instead of full-text search (which matched any filing that mentions the ticker), with the primary document now kept (schema step 4) and an ownership form's styled xsl path mapped to its raw XML so Form4Parser still reads it; held rows from the study import get their document, acceptance time and items filled in when seen again. The news, splits and filings writes move to HistoryWrites, shared by the backfill and the read-through. Verified on the real history database: SOUN filings Sep 1-today took 2 SEC requests then 1 (today only, by design), 912 ms then 88 ms; MTRI's 127 8-Ks served with no request; the latest SOUN Form 4's raw XML fetched and parsed (1 transaction); `gapper radar --date 2026-11-13` twice in a dev Hub (Monitor off) gave identical output, 532 symbols' news marked on the first run and none refetched on the second (212 s then 65 s) (IP-T454); 56267e6e history.backfill.enabled is a registered setting, so `idiotproof settings get/set history.backfill.enabled` works: it was read by HistoryBackfillWorker but missing from SettingsMetadata, and the settings ops refused it as unknown, leaving the history worker with no way to be switched on from the CLI (IP-T454); bc284923 Permanent market history keeps splits and every EDGAR filing: a new ticker's five-year backfill now also stores its Alpaca splits and all of its issuer's filings (every form, Form 4 included, with 8-K items and acceptance time) from the SEC submissions history (new EdgarSubmissions, reading only the older pages that overlap the window; acceptanceDateTime checked to be true UTC against a stored SGML header time), each window marked covered so it is never fetched again (a ticker the SEC list lacks is marked empty; an SEC outage marks nothing). The nightly step adds a market-wide reference pass: one Alpaca request for every split since the last pass, and per EDGAR business day the daily form index (EdgarFormIndex now reads its yyyyMMdd dates) read into each listed filer's submissions, covered under symbol '*', catching up at most ten days and stopping at a failed day. `history backfill --reference [--days N]` runs it by hand. Verified in a dev Hub (Monitor off) on IdiotProof_History: MTRI backfilled end to end (1,255 daily and 123,841 minute bars, 14 news, 0 splits, 405 filings incl. 109 Form 4); the reference pass stored 68 new splits and 2026-11-05..11-11 filings with items and acceptance times. Docs regenerated (also picks up IP-T520's momentum-arm --expire) (IP-T454); 75215fc7 Gapper radar reads after-hours prints: each candidate's last 16:00-19:59 ET SIP trade on the basis session against its regular close, the after-hours high and dollars traded, shown as a new 'after hrs' column and, at +10% on $250k or more, as an 'after hours' reason that scores 0 points until its forward test ends, so the frozen ranking does not move. Finished evenings are cached per basis day under radar\afterhours; an evening still trading is fetched fresh. radar-backtest writes the after-hours fields and the sign. Amendment 06 pre-registers the test before any window data was pulled: sessions 2026-11-11..2027-01-29, risk ratio of a +50% next-session high for AH+ vs AH- candidates, PASS when n >= 30 and the session-bootstrap 90% lower bound > 1; tools/momentum/edge/afterhours_forward.py prints counts only until --final after the window (IP-T501); 494ce8cb Scheduled jobs no longer miss a busy Hub silently: the CLI waits 15 s for /api/health (a down Hub refuses at once; at 3 s machine load got the Hub reported 'not running'), the Hub sets a thread-pool floor of 64, and tools/scheduled-job.ps1 runs each job's idiotproof commands logging output and the real exit code to scheduler-jobs.log. gapper momentum-arm gains --expire and expires flat Momentum pick strategies before arming, so a day's premarket-high levels never carry into the next session (an out-of-hours test run had left three active paper strategies; deactivated, nothing traded) (IP-T520); 6393e1f1 IdiotProof's scheduled steps run through MindAttic.Scheduler (HOUSE-LAW-11): the Hub's own HubScheduler is removed, each step is a jobs.json entry that runs an idiotproof CLI call through the Hub; gapper momentum-arm skips weekends, NYSE holidays and runs after the 15:30 ET entry window, since the Scheduler runs daily jobs every day and catches up missed runs late (IP-T518); faf77f1a Hub service installer pre-fills COMPUTERNAME\user instead of .\user: with a Microsoft-account login the service install only worked as SNOWCRASH\ryand (IP-T519); da5230e0 Hub service installer writes GAPPER_STUDY_DIR into the service environment (the Hub runs the gapper study from C:\Apps) and documents that the 24/7 scheduler only runs where the Monitor is hosted, so the service needs -Monitor (IP-T516); 75852349 The gapper study runs inside the Hub: ResearchHost, a second Core graph wired to the guarded IdiotProof_Research_GAP database (migrated once on first use), gives every `research gappers ...` operation its DI scope through a new dispatcher hook (IOperationScopeRouter), so the trading graph never sees the study; casestudy becomes `research gappers casestudy`; run.ps1 sets GAPPER_STUDY_DIR so the installed Hub finds the study folder. Verified in a dev Hub (Monitor off): `research gappers status` read the research DB (holdout still locked). The tools/GapperStudy, tools/EvidenceSweep and tools/EvidenceRun harnesses are retired, so no process but the Hub opens a database or calls Alpaca; docs regenerated, 292 operations (IP-T515); b99c224a Research helpers go through the Hub: `idiotproof momentum export` writes the calls-vs-reality / edge.py JSON from the Hub (build-artifact.ps1 no longer opens SQL, it fills the template from the Hub's export), `idiotproof gapper radar-backtest` replaces the tool's step, and tools/MomentumTracker is retired (every Momentum. step already runs in the Hub, on the scheduler). The offline gapper-study harness stays the one process opening a database itself, its own guarded research DB only (BIBLE); docs regenerated, 291 operations (IP-T514); 0040e749 Bughunt fixes across the codebase: broker stop fills found again on a non-UTC host (SQL times read as UTC); an order already being sent finishes its diary and audit even if the caller disconnects; the AI panel needs more approvals than rejections; SIP-to-IEX fallback retries the first page; stream sends are serialized and a lost subscription forces a reconnect; options level errors surface; Sandbox fills fractional orders; Ctrl+C on a stream exits 1; keys opt-in is blocked while Paper/Live positions are open; a re-sent market order's --confirm no longer reads as tampered; positions close keeps the broker stop when nothing is sold; prefs risk limits apply at once; trade confirm names non-order codes; backtester trailing/gap-through fills, single AddTarget and seconds in times survive a round trip, short percent stops, ADX seed, Black-Scholes zero-vol and DST expiry, Juneteenth before 2022 and the July 3 early close, ladder rungs no longer switch off later exits; news backfills and windows are covered only as far as they were read, catalyst freshness at receipt, holidays skipped in replays, the current EDGAR quarter is re-read, rejected chunks retried per symbol, transient failures not cached, validation/holdout refuse in-sample config choice, catalyst intake restarts cleanly; a post-decision feature leak, an entry-bar stop and a split direction in the study code; edge.py counts each pick once and groups by trade date (IP-T505); 4052c3e7 Hub scheduler: the Hub runs the research and arming steps 24/7 on an ET schedule as ordinary operations through its own dispatcher (caller "scheduler", ledgered and echoed like a CLI call): momentum import/extract through the evening and morning, verify and report, gapper radar into the "Gapper radar" Alpaca paper watchlist (saved under D:\IdiotProofData\radar), and at 09:29:30 ET gapper momentum-arm --activate (Paper, 1 share). Only the Hub hosting the Monitor schedules; IDIOTPROOF_HUB_SCHEDULER=0 turns it off. gapper radar gains --watchlist and --save (risk Write); CLI/MCP docs regenerated, 289 operations. Also bughunt IP-T505: the Hub pins an invariant culture (IP-T512); cbc1ea60 Decimal arguments refuse an ambiguous comma group: "1,005" (1005 or 1.005?) and "0,001" are refused with a hint, "1,005.00", "1005" and "1.005" bind; editing an index event's effective date updates its claim in place (identity = ticker, index, action, announced date) instead of adding a duplicate and leaving the TBA claim Pending (IP-T511); 00df1871 Gapper study universe: the unexplained-move guard reads only bars before D, so a >+200% close on D (the outcome) no longer excludes the biggest runners and the 25 days after them (IP-T510); b91f69a3 Regulatory scanner pages through every Federal Register SRO notice since the window start (publication-date filter, 100 per page, up to 20 pages) instead of the newest 40, and the scan pass advances its regulatory-scan-ran marker only when the whole window was read; the EDGAR latest-filings poller pages each form back (up to 5 x 100) until a page holds only filings already seen, and logs a failed feed instead of skipping it silently. Also bughunt IP-T505: research claims are dated by the ET day (IP-T509); 1b2d7e2c Momentum. ticker resolution uses only what was known when the video went up: variants and the mover bonus come from the prior session's movers, no longer from the trade day's own runners (look-ahead that resolved misheard tickers toward stocks that ran). New `momentum reresolve` re-resolves every stored claim without re-running the LLM, rebuilds the levels of a claim whose symbol changes and drops its outcome for re-verify; tools/MomentumTracker gains the step. Also bughunt IP-T505: today's partial movers table is no longer cached, "twenty five bucks" reads as $25, and a malformed channel-list entry no longer aborts the import (IP-T508); 7888bf8a Risk Guardian restores today's realized loss from the trade diary when it is first built, so a Hub restart mid-day no longer resets the daily circuit breaker (IP-LAW-2) to $0; SeedDailyLoss never lowers a total already counted (IP-T507); fe1771c1 Monitor order tracking: every Monitor entry and exit carries a client order id naming its strategy (ipe-/ipx-, like the protective stops' ips-). An exit is booked only for what actually filled, at the real average price; one still resting after ~3s is cancelled and nothing is booked, so the next tick re-protects the position and retries (it used to be booked as sold after the broker stop was withdrawn). A stale entry is cleared only after this strategy's own working entry order is cancelled and confirmed unfilled. A broker call that threw is resolved by looking the order up by its id, not by guessing from positions (no second entry while the first is still working). Same files also carry bughunt IP-T505 fixes: early-close days stay active through the 1-5 PM extended session, a failed bar refresh keeps managing exits on cached bars, limits below $1 round to 4 decimals, and a broker holding no more than the exit sells books a full exit (IP-T506)) | cf6e9eed |

The gapper radar's catalyst news, ResearchService (8-K, Form 4, news) and the research scan pass use it. Filings come from the issuer's SEC submissions history instead of full-text search (which matched any filing that mentions the ticker), with the primary document now kept (schema step 4) and an ownership form's styled xsl path mapped to its raw XML so Form4Parser still reads it; held rows from the study import get their document, acceptance time and items filled in when seen again. (landed on main since the last green run: tickets IP-T528, IP-T539, IP-T506, IP-T530, IP-T523, IP-T525, IP-T487, IP-T527, IP-T521, IP-T447, IP-T454, IP-T520, IP-T501, IP-T518, IP-T519, IP-T516, IP-T515, IP-T514, IP-T505, IP-T512, IP-T511 in 6fc8395c The LLM gate is not re-asked every tick after it says no: a strategy whose entry conditions stayed true polled the voter panel every few seconds until one run approved (the IP-T528 paper proof: 20+ vetoes in three minutes, 3-4 LLM calls each, then an order on the first Approve). After a non-approval the Monitor leaves the panel alone for that strategy for 2 minutes, doubling with each refusal in a row up to 15; an approval clears the streak and one older than 30 minutes starts over. While waiting it writes no signal-fire row, and the signal-vetoed audit row says when the panel is asked again. The wait is in memory (a Monitor restart allows one fresh vote) and is not yet shown in ConditionProgress, which still reads ALL PASS during it. Built only (IP-T539); 33ff625f Monitor measures a position from the broker's real fill, not the entry's limit price: an entry is booked at its limit when the order is placed, and nothing moved it to the fill afterwards, so the IP-T528 paper proof's 1 MSFT bought with a 506.12 marketable limit and filled at 505.23 had its row, audit line and diary at 506.12 and its 1% stop and target measured from there. In the hold phase the Monitor now looks up its own finished entry order (ipe- client id) at most every 15 s, and once per booking sets LastEntryPrice and the open diary row to the average fill price, with an entry-price-corrected audit row; an order still working, unlisted, or a broker that cannot be asked keeps the booked price (gives up after 10 minutes), and the filled quantity stays the stale-entry path's business (IP-T506). Built only; no harness test added, and the installed Hub does not have it until the next publish (IP-T530); e9a14253 Self-repair 1, errors carry the fix as data: an IdiotScript diagnostic now carries a ScriptFix (code, offset, length, line, column, replacement, description) when exactly one correct edit exists, and ScriptDiagnostics.Repair applies them and offers the whole corrected script only after it re-analyzes with no error and parses (a few passes, since one fix can expose the next problem). Fixed: IPS001 a misspelled verb with one closest match, IPS002 an unclosed '(' around plain values, IPS003 an extra ')' after a ')', IPS004 an unterminated plain string argument, IPS006 a number in quotes or with '$', IPS008/IPS010 arguments the parser ignores, IPS013 a missing EndIf(). No fix where it would be a guess: IPS005, IPS007 (every verb with a default already takes it as optional), IPS009, IPS011/012/014/015/016, IPS020-025. dsl validate and dsl parse return fixes and corrected_script and still judge the text as written; the new --fix opt-in makes the corrected script the result. An import error carries the same payload (DslRepairData); nothing that saves or activates a strategy applies a fix. On the API side every binding failure is a BindError with a CallChange when determinable, and when every problem has one and the corrected call binds again the usage error carries a CallFix (operation, command_line, argv, args, changes) in UsageErrorData: operation, option and JSON key names with one closest match, a positional passed as --name, enum values one typo from one accepted value, whole numbers written 5.0 or 1_000, dates in another unambiguous form, times as 0930 or 9am, y/n flags. Never corrected: a missing required value, a word for a number, 03/04/2026, any number with a comma (1,005 stays refused), two equally close names. Built only; no harness test added, and the installed Hub does not have it until the next publish (IP-T530); e9a14253 Self-repair 1, errors carry the fix as data: an IdiotScript diagnostic now carries a ScriptFix (code, offset, length, line, column, replacement, description) when exactly one correct edit exists, and ScriptDiagnostics.Repair applies them and offers the whole corrected script only after it re-analyzes with no error and parses (a few passes, since one fix can expose the next problem). Fixed: IPS001 a misspelled verb with one closest match, IPS002 an unclosed '(' around plain values, IPS003 an extra ')' after a ')', IPS004 an unterminated plain string argument, IPS006 a number in quotes or with '$', IPS008/IPS010 arguments the parser ignores, IPS013 a missing EndIf(). No fix where it would be a guess: IPS005, IPS007 (every verb with a default already takes it as optional), IPS009, IPS011/012/014/015/016, IPS020-025. dsl validate and dsl parse return fixes and corrected_script and still judge the text as written; the new --fix opt-in makes the corrected script the result. An import error carries the same payload (DslRepairData); nothing that saves or activates a strategy applies a fix. On the API side every binding failure is a BindError with a CallChange when determinable, and when every problem has one and the corrected call binds again the usage error carries a CallFix (operation, command_line, argv, args, changes) in UsageErrorData: operation, option and JSON key names with one closest match, a positional passed as --name, enum values one typo from one accepted value, whole numbers written 5.0 or 1_000, dates in another unambiguous form, times as 0930 or 9am, y/n flags. Never corrected: a missing required value, a word for a number, 03/04/2026, any number with a comma (1,005 stays refused), two equally close names. The dispatcher never runs the corrected call, and it is printed from the result text rather than the message so the command ledger does not keep a copy of every argument value. CLI/MCP docs regenerated for dsl parse and dsl validate only (the other stale entries belong to tickets in flight). Verified by building IdiotProof.slnx and by a throwaway console against the built assemblies: 26 scripts through Repair, both dsl operations with and without --fix, and the binder and dispatcher cases the new tests assert; the tests themselves were not run (IP-T523); 0ec4e02b Quarantine auto-repair: the Monitor repairs a flat, quarantined strategy canon from its own stored script when nothing is lost, and lifts the quarantine itself. The rule is CanonRepair.Plan (Core/Services): the canon is present and rejected by the strict reader; the script has no error diagnostics and parses; the re-derived canon passes the strict reader, reads back byte for byte and is for the same symbol; the stored canon is a schema-1 JSON object so it can be counted; step by step the new canon has no fewer entry, While or ThenWhen conditions, conditional blocks, branches, branch conditions, branch exits or take-profit targets, every exit rule and entry gate the stored one set, no fewer steps, and the same session, direction, quantity and notional; the row holds no position and is at step 1 of its sequence. StrategyRepository.RepairQuarantinedCanonAsync is the only writer: it re-checks the fresh row, writes ScriptJson and UpdatedUtc only, and saves the strategy-repaired audit row (quarantine reason, changes, canon before and after) in the same SaveChanges. The Monitor calls it from the flat-quarantine branch of EvaluateOneAsync, after checking the switches and that no order tagged with the strategy is working at its broker; it attempts once per quarantine reason (reason, canon and script), looks again at state refusals every 5 minutes, re-reads the row through the strict reader after a write and never evaluates it in that tick. Settings quarantine.autorepair.enabled (default true: Paper and Sandbox) and quarantine.autorepair.live (default false: a Live canon is not rewritten unless set), both registered in SettingsMetadata. strategy quarantine now says for each strategy what blocks an automatic repair and shows the proposed repair, with --diff for the line diff; the CLI/MCP docs and the catalog carry that change, BIBLE IP-LAW-8/11 and the digest describe the repair. Verified by building (every project compiles; the Cli and Hub output copy was locked by a running dev Hub) and by running the rule, the repository write and the operation against EF InMemory rows in a scratch console (20 rule cases, 5 repository calls, the operation output); the Monitor path and the new tests are built only, not run (IP-T525); a108a279 Gapper study amendment 07, registered before any replay: two long-only multi-step gapper templates built on Steps (classic-gapper ride, flat into the bell, then a second leg on the first higher low above VWAP 09:35-10:30, or on a retest of the pre-bell high with speed 09:31-09:40 and out by 09:44) are replayed by the shared StrategyBacktester on the study's train days only, against the single-step classic gapper on the same symbol-days, net of the frozen cost model per leg; a template passes only with >= +1.0% net per run and a day-clustered lower bound above 0, 150 runs on 40 days, 150 later legs, 3 of 4 folds, a paired gain over the baseline and DSR >= 0.95. No grid, 3 ledger trials. The code that runs it (`research gappers explore --command gapper-sequences`) and the templates (GapperSequenceTemplates, shown by `strategy samples`, 1 share, valid and round-tripping in a dev Hub) are in this commit; nothing was replayed before it. A third day-two template ships as a sample only and is not evaluated. The detector that survived (H11p) is frozen by the new `research gappers detector-export` into Catalogs/formation-detector.json, refit exactly as its validation run (weighted, train only, holdout never read); on export it reproduced the reported weighted AUC 0.912 vs benchmark 0.558 on the same 107,669 validation rows (253,115 train rows) and records each input's train missing share. FormationDetector (Evidence) holds the feature list and row transform now shared by the study's H11/H11p code and the live scorer. At 08:00 ET the recorder scores its universe (FormationDetectorScorer), stores detectorScore on each row and writes one formation-alert audit row with the top 10; its snapshots now also get the reverse-split and 424B/S-1 inputs the study's carried, from the permanent history (FormationReferenceSource, the snapshot stage's rules, cached 10 min). `gapper formation shadow` is the pre-registered 20-session paper shadow (gapper study amendment 06): live rows labeled with the study's own reach label (GapperStudyLabeler.Reach, now shared), detector vs catalyst-latency benchmark AUC with a day-clustered 95% lower bound > 0, and no input missing live 20 points more often than in training. `gapper formation status` shows the detector. Verified in a dev Hub (Monitor off): export, status line and an empty shadow; the live 08:00 path runs only once the recorder is enabled (IP-T447); 22d08560 News and SEC filings read through the permanent history like bars do: HistoryReadThrough serves what IdiotProof_History covers, fetches only uncovered finished ET days (stored and marked covered) and always fetches the current day live (stored, never marked); a stopped history server falls back to the live calls unstored. The gapper radar's catalyst news, ResearchService (8-K, Form 4, news) and the research scan pass use it. Filings come from the issuer's SEC submissions history instead of full-text search (which matched any filing that mentions the ticker), with the primary document now kept (schema step 4) and an ownership form's styled xsl path mapped to its raw XML so Form4Parser still reads it; held rows from the study import get their document, acceptance time and items filled in when seen again. The news, splits and filings writes move to HistoryWrites, shared by the backfill and the read-through. Verified on the real history database: SOUN filings Sep 1-today took 2 SEC requests then 1 (today only, by design), 912 ms then 88 ms; MTRI's 127 8-Ks served with no request; the latest SOUN Form 4's raw XML fetched and parsed (1 transaction); `gapper radar --date 2026-11-13` twice in a dev Hub (Monitor off) gave identical output, 532 symbols' news marked on the first run and none refetched on the second (212 s then 65 s) (IP-T454); 56267e6e history.backfill.enabled is a registered setting, so `idiotproof settings get/set history.backfill.enabled` works: it was read by HistoryBackfillWorker but missing from SettingsMetadata, and the settings ops refused it as unknown, leaving the history worker with no way to be switched on from the CLI (IP-T454); bc284923 Permanent market history keeps splits and every EDGAR filing: a new ticker's five-year backfill now also stores its Alpaca splits and all of its issuer's filings (every form, Form 4 included, with 8-K items and acceptance time) from the SEC submissions history (new EdgarSubmissions, reading only the older pages that overlap the window; acceptanceDateTime checked to be true UTC against a stored SGML header time), each window marked covered so it is never fetched again (a ticker the SEC list lacks is marked empty; an SEC outage marks nothing). The nightly step adds a market-wide reference pass: one Alpaca request for every split since the last pass, and per EDGAR business day the daily form index (EdgarFormIndex now reads its yyyyMMdd dates) read into each listed filer's submissions, covered under symbol '*', catching up at most ten days and stopping at a failed day. `history backfill --reference [--days N]` runs it by hand. Verified in a dev Hub (Monitor off) on IdiotProof_History: MTRI backfilled end to end (1,255 daily and 123,841 minute bars, 14 news, 0 splits, 405 filings incl. 109 Form 4); the reference pass stored 68 new splits and 2026-11-05..11-11 filings with items and acceptance times. Finished evenings are cached per basis day under radar\afterhours; an evening still trading is fetched fresh. radar-backtest writes the after-hours fields and the sign.
